title: Gandhar Oil Refinery (India) Ltd - 544029 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Gandhar Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to INR1,093 crore, with FY26 PAT at INR137 crore and EBITDA margin about 5.5-6%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR1,093 crore (up 14% YoY) and Q4 EBITDA was INR64 crore, up both QoQ and YoY, with PAT of INR37 crore versus INR12 crore a year earlier. FY26 revenue reached INR4,241 crore (about 9-10% growth), EBITDA INR234 crore and PAT INR137 crore. Operating cash flow improved to INR127.77 crore from INR14.71 crore. Management said Middle East disruption (Strait of Hormuz) caused base oil price volatility and freight pressure, but pass-through pricing and sourcing changes mitigated the impact. Plants ran above nameplate capacity on a multi-shift basis, and Taloja land and a South Africa subsidiary were flagged as future growth steps without firm capex numbers.

segments.name: PHPO (personal care, healthcare, performance oil)
segments.commentary: About 50% of revenue; management calls it the company's core focus, with a stated growth rate of about 4% CAGR over the next 4-5 years (as stated on the call).

segments.name: PIO (process industry oils)
segments.commentary: About 10.19% of revenue in FY26. Transformer oil is also part of the mix, but no separate margin or price trend was disclosed.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports were about 42.8% of consolidated revenue in the prepared remarks, and about 45% in Q&A (range given as 45-48%). Sales go to 100+ countries. US exposure is described as minimal.

guidance_outlook: Management expects consolidated EBITDA margin of about 6% to be maintained in coming quarters, but gave no hard numeric target.
Management is working on a two-year capacity expansion plan; capex budget clarity is expected in the next 2-3 quarters.
Debt-to-equity is practically nil standalone; management expects to maintain it except for any borrowing for the South Africa expansion.
Management said it is open to inorganic growth opportunities.
Volume growth of close to double digits has been historical; management expects revenue growth to continue, but declined to give formal multi-year guidance.
capex_capacity: India plants (Taloja and Silvassa) installed capacity is 3,62,100 kL on a 2-shift basis; output was 4,58,853 kL, about 125-126% utilisation, using 3-shift operation in some months.
Group installed capacity is 5,97,403 kL including Sharjah (Texol, Hamriyah Free Zone). Output of 5,54,212 kL gives about 93% utilisation.
Sharjah (Texol) is underutilised due to port and shipping disruption; management expects utilisation to ramp up once the situation normalises.

A plot of land was bought at Taloja for plant expansion. Management said the Taloja facility is close to 100% utilised. Panvel land acquisition was referenced by an analyst but not discussed by management.

Board has given broad approval for a South Africa investment (analyst cited INR50 crore); the company has only just set up a South African entity and has not decided between office and plant. No investment is planned yet, per management.
demand_pricing: Management described the global white oil market as about USD1.93 billion in 2026, rising to about USD2.75 billion by 2033 (about 5.5% CAGR), led by Asia Pacific.
Base oil prices rose about 20-25% in the past month versus about 10% for crude, per management. Pricing is mostly index-linked or spot, with fortnightly price revisions to customers.
Pass-through contracts cover about 35-40% of customers; the rest are repriced through fortnightly revisions.

Raw material sourcing: about 20-22% comes from Middle East suppliers. Sourcing has shifted toward Korean suppliers and domestic refiners (BPCL, IOCL). Suppliers including Aramco and ADNOC are reportedly supplying via alternate routes.
Freight: most export sales are FOB, and CFR shipments pass freight through at current rates, per management. Red Sea routing has added transit time.

qa_highlights.question: How has the Middle East disruption affected sourcing, freight and customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material supply has been uninterrupted through contracts with suppliers, with some added transit time. Sales to Africa, the US and Europe are unaffected, and only the Middle East route is affected. Export is about 45% of revenue and domestic about 54%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and can it reach the FY23 peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims to maintain about 6% consolidated EBITDA margin and will try to improve, but gave no numeric target for the 7-8% FY22-23 levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and capex headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: India plants ran at about 125-126% of 2-shift nameplate capacity, with 3-shift use in some months. Group utilisation is about 93%. Capex plans are to be drawn up over the next 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the realisations by product and the margin per kL?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 average realisation was INR76,526 per kL across products; PHPO was about INR78,000 per kL. FY26 EBITDA was INR8,696 per kL, and Q4 gross margin spread was INR9,351 per kL.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company handle the cash needs of planned expansion and South Africa?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is debt-free standalone and has reserves and surplus of about INR1,200 crore (clarified from INR1,500 crore). Management said operating cash flow of INR127 crore could fund an expansion of about INR100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can costs be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin improved through the year, which shows that price increases have been passed on. It said price increases are passed on to customers via contracts and repricing.

risks_watch: Strait of Hormuz disruption and Middle East war could keep base oil, freight and insurance costs volatile, and affect the Texol (Sharjah) plant's raw material and port access.
Sharjah (Texol) under-utilisation and a March 2026 revenue impact from raw material shortages.
Operating cash flow was described by an analyst as inconsistent, and working capital (inventory of about 40-45 days) will need to be watched.
Capex plan and South Africa investment details are still pending; the investment size, plant versus office decision and expansion budget remain unclear.
Management did not give a transformer oil price trend or a segment-wise margin breakdown, and said it would revert on R&D spend (about 4-5% of other expenses, per CFO).
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth, cash flow and debt position, but evasive on forward guidance, capex size, South Africa scope, and segment margins, which were deferred to later updates.
key_quotes: Our cash flow from the operations stood at a positive INR127.77 crores as of 31st March 2026 compared to INR14.71 crores in the previous year, reflecting a stronger operating efficiency and working capital management.

So the company is purely focused on its customers and demand from its customers based on which we have been maintaining an optimum inven tory level of around –40-45 days, looking at the current geopolitical situation.

So once there is an official agreement with the customer in terms of sale purchases, then in terms of service, in terms of quality, if this are streamlined, then the customers are all long-term customers.
